name: Kuwait

campaign_state.basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Kuwait were reported in 2026. No end to the wider war is reported, so the classification is uncertain, and uncertain is treated as active.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on the date checked. A search that returns no recent report does not show that none occurred. Iteration 20 added four conflict-level searches (the wider war, the Gulf states as a group, Iraq). None reported an end of the war, and renewed hostilities were reported in the autumn of 2026. No facility was looked up.

no_index_reason: Only the Russia-theatre system has a disruption index. Its weights and recovery assumptions were designed for that theatre and are not transferred to other countries, so this page shows reported disruptions and national energy context instead. No index is not a zero.

sectors.reason: A national capacity total is published in a secondary compilation (EIA, 2023), but the country has very few refineries, so a share of capacity affected would be the status of a named plant. Shown as national context only.
sectors.label: Refining

sectors.reason: A national installed-capacity total is available (EIA, 2024), but the ministry's statistical yearbook, which would give a dated national inventory on one basis, could not be opened: its page shows covers for 2017 to 2019 with no file. No outage reporting exists, the list of plants is short, and attack events resolve to country level. No model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).
sectors.label: Electric generation

sectors.reason: National aggregates only; the event-burden measure does not fit, and no grid detail is collected.
sectors.label: Transmission burden

sectors.reason: No inventory is built: it would centre on export terminals and routing, which are out of scope. No recent national crude export figure with clear reuse terms was read; the gap is stated, not filled.
sectors.label: Oil logistics & export

sectors.reason: National dry gas production, consumption and imports are published (EIA, 2024) and shown as context. Gas processing and gas import are concentrated in very few places, so a share of capacity affected would be the status of particular facilities. No facility capacity is recorded.
sectors.label: Gas

sectors.reason: No coal production in 2024 and no coal in power generation (EIA). A small coal consumption is recorded (about 0.003 quadrillion Btu in 2024); its use is not stated and was not researched, so this is not marked as not applicable.
sectors.label: Coal

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_note: The state oil companies and the electricity and water ministry disclose disruption through statements, mostly carried by the state news agency and the daily press. No body publishes an outage register or reliability statistics, the ministry's own news archive is thin before late 2024, and the oil companies' statement listings cannot be enumerated by an ordinary request, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: Six governorates (muhafazah), which is also what Natural Earth draws (KW-AH, KW-FA, KW-HA, KW-JA, KW-KU, KW-MU). The count of six was not confirmed on an official page this session: the government portal returned HTTP 403 and the statistics bureau's home page does not state it. Attacks and sabotage are recorded at COUNTRY level, with no governorate, facility or operator, because a governorate and a class together would name the facility. Other events are placed by governorate. Offshore events are country level and are never snapped to the nearest coast.

rulings.note: Al Ahmadi as drawn reaches the southern international boundary. Natural Earth draws no separate unit for the Saudi-Kuwaiti Partitioned (Neutral) Zone: it draws the boundary that divides the zone, and the part north of that line lies inside this polygon. An onshore event reported in the zone is placed by the drawn boundary (this unit, or the Saudi system) where the source makes the side clear, and at country level otherwise. Shared onshore and offshore fields are never a unit of analysis. A statement about the map file, not about resource rights or sovereignty.
Al Jahrah is drawn as three separate polygons; all are this unit. Waters and offshore installations lie outside every governorate polygon, and this system makes no statement on maritime boundaries.
The Capital Governorate (Al Asimah, العاصمة), under the code Natural Earth carries. The map file draws it as two separate polygons; both are this unit.

precision_policy.reason: Kuwait's refineries, export terminals and most large power and water plants sit in two or three governorates, so a governorate and a class together name the facility. Attacks and sabotage are recorded for the country, with no governorate, facility or operator. Other events are placed by governorate.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Kuwait source-audit lane (iteration 19). CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read in this session, from the local copy of EIA's bulk file (release 2026-10-16) or from EIA's country brief page; vintages are mixed (2023-2025) and stated per row, and must not be combined into one 'current' picture. No value is later than a 2025 annual total, and none describes the state of any facility. All rows are country totals on EIA's definitions: crude includes lease condensate, dry gas is marketed gas less extraction loss, electricity is net. Capacities are installed or nameplate figures and say nothing about operation. No national Kuwaiti statistical source could be opened with readable terms, so none is cited. Crude exports are ABSENT, not zero: EIA's export series stops at 2018 and no other source with clear terms was read. National aggregates only: no facility, plant, terminal or route figure is recorded. See docs/countries/KW_SOURCE_AUDIT.md. 2 figures newer than 2024 are withheld while the campaign policy applies.

significance: Petroleum and other liquids made up 88.8% of Kuwait's primary energy production in 2024 and natural gas 11.1%; coal production was zero (EIA).
Kuwait produced 2.58 million barrels per day of crude oil including lease condensate in 2025 (EIA).

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: One automated visit to each cited page. Blocked means the site refused an automated visitor, not that the page is gone. Redirects to a home page or listing count as gone; redirects to a bot check count as blocked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
